clue.text: That fellow and I in Texas possibly dither

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the single letter goes inside the word for Texas's kind of place

blocks.note: the pronoun for that fellow
Texas is one example of a US state
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man and the speaker, somewhere in Texas, cannot make up their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks Texas as just one example of a state, so the definition-by-example is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to be indecisive, a close synonym of the verb meaning to pause in doubt.

clue.text: Entertainer — spooky individual, no good

indicators.note: no means without, so that letter is taken away from the word before

blocks.note: a ghost is a spooky being
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A performer described as an eerie character who is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A host entertains guests, at a party or on a television show, so is one who entertains.

clue.text: Tries hard in Cornish town, with river invading

indicators.note: an invader goes into territory, so the letter for river pushes inside the town's name

blocks.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, England's south-western county
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone makes a big effort in a Cornish resort when a river floods in.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make great efforts, so 'tries hard' is an exact synonym in the same verb form.

clue.text: A celebrant's moving around centres of worship

indicators.note: letters moving around shift out of their places into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, with the S of the possessive: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A priest's procession goes round the various churches.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a place of worship, such as a chapel or meeting house, or the Hebrews' sacred tent.

clue.text: Diplomacy reportedly fixed

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: tact is diplomacy, and it is pronounced the same as the past tense of the verb meaning pinned

explanation.surface: A news report says the diplomatic negotiations were rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' in the surface suggests rigged; here it means fastened with small nails.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack something is to fasten it with tacks or loose stitches, so tacked means fixed in place.

clue.text: Posh vehicle some two miles back

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run that sits inside them
going back means the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A smart car is parked a couple of miles behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests distance, but 'two miles' is just the string of letters to look inside, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine, shortened in speech, is the large luxurious car associated with wealthy passengers.

clue.text: Arctic inhabitant wearing two-piece maybe, with head covered

indicators.note: a covered head is hidden from view, so the first letter of the garment disappears

blocks.note: dressed in something is wearing it
a two-piece is one kind of suit

explanation.surface: A northern local dressed in a two-piece outfit, with a hood up against the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inuit are the indigenous people of the Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland and Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are native peoples of the Arctic, so one of them is an inhabitant of that region.

clue.text: Old boy vile ultimately — is worker courteously deferential?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the last letter of vile
taken as written
a worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: Asking whether a nasty former pupil now employed is properly respectful.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant describes someone showing obeisance, a respectful bow or submission, so polite and deferential.

clue.text: Keep quiet and stroke plant

blocks.note: the hushing sound telling someone to keep quiet
to stroke something is to rub it gently

explanation.surface: Instructions for tending a houseplant: say nothing and caress it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush is a woody plant smaller than a tree, so the answer is one kind of plant.

clue.text: Attire was expensive for yours truly, having to appear outside university

indicators.note: the first phrase is placed around the outside of the following letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: 'it cost me' says it was expensive for the speaker, and yours truly is the speaker
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone complains that an outfit set them back a lot because they had to be seen beyond the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is a jokey way of saying 'me', so the phrase read plainly is 'cost me'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit worn for a role or occasion is clothing, which is what attire means.

clue.text: Depression limited by calm ability to make lucky discoveries

indicators.note: a thing limited by another is bounded by it on both sides, so the first word goes inside

blocks.note: serenity is a state of calm
a dip is a hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: Low mood held in check by a peaceful talent for happy finds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low spirits, but it is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is the knack of finding pleasant things by chance, coined by Horace Walpole.

clue.text: Various characters in street brave, not spineless types

indicators.note: letters described as various are mixed up rather than kept in their printed order

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rough street full of assorted tough characters, none of them cowards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spineless' in the surface means cowardly; in the definition it is literal, animals that have a backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals with a backbone are, literally, creatures that are not without a spine.

clue.text: Son making fun of fancy work in attire?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
mocking is making fun of someone

explanation.surface: A boy teasing someone about their elaborate clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy work' looks like flashy clothing, but it is decorative needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: Smocking is ornamental stitching that gathers fabric into tight pleats, a kind of embroidery on garments.

clue.text: Onset of merriment with American jazz fan in port

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of merriment
US is short for the United States, so American
cat is old jazz slang for an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A cheerful American jazz lover arrives in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' as a jazz fan is 1930s-40s swing slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital and chief seaport of Oman, on the Gulf of Oman.

clue.text: Bit of fun I so need in style of singing

indicators.note: only a bit of the following run of words is used, a piece lying inside them

blocks.note: the letters running from the second of fun to the first of need

explanation.surface: A choir member says a little enjoyment is needed in the way they sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing in unison means all voices sing the same melody together, a manner of choral performance.

clue.text: Italian title some officials ignored

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a run of letters lying inside them is used

blocks.note: the letters from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: An Italian honorific that certain bureaucrats chose to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Signore is the Italian form of address equivalent to Mr or sir.

clue.text: Following sun initially, I go wrong on a mountain range

indicators.note: initially points to the very start of the word, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of sun
taken as written
to err is to go wrong
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hiker, after setting off at sunrise, gets lost in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' and 'on' place the pieces one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, the Spanish word as in Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Arriving across flat territory and grumbling

indicators.note: one word stretching across another means it surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: arriving is coming
a plain is a stretch of flat land

explanation.surface: Travellers crossing a dull flat landscape moan all the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaining means expressing dissatisfaction, which is what grumbling is.

clue.text: Tree fellow hugs quietly

indicators.note: hugging something means wrapping round it, so the word for fellow surrounds the letter

blocks.note: a fellow is a male
p (piano) is the musical instruction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A tree-hugger quietly embracing a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a broadleaved tree, source of syrup and of the leaf on Canada's flag.

clue.text: Something that helps motorist travel round ancient city

definitions.text: Something that helps motorist travel round

blocks.clueFragment: Something that helps motorist travel round
blocks.note: first meaning: the rubber ring on a wheel that rolls a car along
second meaning: the old Phoenician port, now in Lebanon

explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a route around the city, but it belongs to the first meaning: the thing goes round.

clue.text: Claim of artist's model who enforces ideas on others?

blocks.note: first reading: an artist's model poses, so might claim to be a poser, split as two words
second meaning: a person who forces views onto other people

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is read as a two-word sentence, 'I'm poser', said by someone who sits for a painter; the whole runs together into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: One who imposes things on other people, such as rules or opinions, is by definition an imposer.

clue.text: Form of humour — smoother and nasty ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of that word is kept

blocks.note: an iron smooths creases out of clothes
the last letter of nasty

explanation.surface: Describing a comic style that is both slick and spiteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoother' looks like a comparative adjective, but here it is a noun: a device that smooths.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is a mode of humour that says the opposite of what is meant, a recognised comic form.

clue.text: Information about lake in Scottish valley

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word wraps around the single letter

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A tourist leaflet about a loch in a Highland valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, the word used especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Beautiful boy regularly meddled on article in gym

indicators.note: one thing in another means the short word sits inside the exercise hall
taking letters regularly means every other one, at even intervals
one piece placed on another is added to it, so the alternate letters are attached after the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
an is the indefinite article
the second, fourth and sixth letters of meddled

explanation.surface: A handsome lad kept interfering with an item of equipment at the fitness centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganymede is the Trojan youth of Greek myth, carried off by Zeus for his beauty to be cupbearer of the gods. 'on' places the alternate letters after the gym piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ganymede was the most handsome of mortals, so beautiful that Zeus took him to Olympus.
